title: Size limits: decimal width 38; strings and blobs 4 GiB - 1; vectors 128 GB
verdict: decimal width over 38, a string or blob over 2^32 - 1 bytes and a vector over 128 GB raise OutOfRange
description: Decimals: a width must be 1 to 38; addition, subtraction and multiplication raise when the result needs a width over 38, and a declared value out of bounds is rejected by the binder (numeric types page).

Strings: the text page says a declared length `VARCHAR(n)` has no effect, and names no maximum. Lists, arrays, structs and maps: the list page names no maximum length or depth. The parser's `max_expression_depth` (default 1000) limits nesting of expressions; raising it risks a stack overflow (configuration page).

Source at v2.0.0: a string or blob (`string_t`) has a 32-bit length, `MAX_STRING_SIZE` = 2^32 - 1 bytes. Every string built in a vector's heap (`StringVector::EmptyString`, `AddBlob`) goes through `StringHeap::CreateEmptyStringInHeap`, which raises an `OutOfRangeException` past it ("Cannot create a string of size …"), so `repeat`, `concat` and the like raise rather than wrap. Lists and maps (`list_entry_t`) have 64-bit offsets and lengths; their child vector grows through the standard vector buffer, which raises an `OutOfRangeException` past 128 GB (`MAX_VECTOR_SIZE` = 2^37 bytes) for one vector. An out-of-range error is an execution error, so `TRY` turns it into NULL (duckdb-exec-try).
reference: The reference caps decimals at 38 digits and raises past them (`docs/reference-semantics.md`, decimal arithmetic). It has no limit on string, blob or list lengths.

evidence.note: heap strings past MAX_STRING_SIZE raise OutOfRangeException
resizing a vector past MAX_VECTOR_SIZE raises OutOfRangeException
a list's child reserves through the child vector

provenance.checked_by: characterization pipeline round 3 (engine tests; aggregates, windows, relations, temporal, nested, strings, execution)

evidence.note: LPAD/RPAD to 1100000000 four-byte characters, or 2147483647 characters → Out of Range Error: maximum supported string size
TRANSLATE(repeat('a', 1100000000), 'a', '😀') → Out of Range Error: maximum supported string size
length(string_agg) of 30 strings of 10^8 bytes → 3000000000, below 2^32
repeat([1], 99999999999999999) → maximum allowed vector size; a length product that wraps uint64 → Out of Range Error
LIST_RESIZE to 9999999999999999999 or 4000999999999999999 → maximum allowed vector size
substring offsets outside [-2^32, 2^32) and lengths of 2^32 or more → Out of Range Error
'0.1'::DECIMAL(40) → Binder Error: width must be between 1 and 38
the sum of a DECIMAL is a DECIMAL(38) and raises Overflow in SUM of DECIMAL past it

provenance.notes: Read at tag v2.0.0 (commit d54cbbe3); the tests were not run. The tests pin the string limit (results past 2^32 - 1 bytes raise, a 3·10^9-byte string is fine), the vector limit for lists, substring's 32-bit offsets and the 38-digit decimal width.
